questions.q: Why do picklists, validation rules, and duplicate rules all need to be active together rather than relying on just one?
options: Salesforce requires all three to be configured before any one of them works
Only duplicate rules actually affect data quality — the others are cosmetic
Each catches a different kind of failure; none of them substitutes for the others
They must be activated in a specific order or none of them will save
questions.explain: Picklists prevent bad entry, validation rules block incomplete saves, and duplicate rules catch near-matches — a gap in one layer isn't covered by the others.

questions.q: Why import a small test batch of 10-20 rows before running a full bulk import?
options: Salesforce enforces a hard limit of 20 test rows before any import
A systematic error, like a mis-mapped column, is far cheaper to catch and fix in a small batch than across thousands of live rows
Test batches are required to activate duplicate rules
It permanently disables validation rules for the rest of the import
questions.explain: A small test batch surfaces mapping or formatting problems while they're still cheap to fix, before they're baked into a much larger import.

questions.q: What does it mean to say "data quality needs an owner"?
options: Someone needs to actively review Duplicate Record Sets, tune matching criteria, and audit picklists on an ongoing basis, not just configure features once
Only the system administrator profile is allowed to view data quality reports
A dedicated Data Quality object must be created before any rules can run
Ownership is a field that must be populated on every record
questions.explain: Rules and picklists are necessary but not sufficient — without someone reviewing reports and tuning criteria over time, quality decays even with every feature turned on.

questions.q: An org has validation rules, duplicate rules, and State/Country Picklists active, but new data still looks inconsistent after six months. What's the most likely gap?
options: Validation rules and duplicate rules cannot be active in the same org
State/Country Picklists disable all other data quality tools automatically
The org needs to delete and recreate all picklist fields
No one is reviewing reports or tuning the rules on an ongoing basis — the features exist but lack an owner
questions.explain: Features alone decay in effectiveness without a recurring review rhythm — false positives go untuned, Duplicate Record Sets pile up unreviewed, and picklist values drift.

questions.q: Why should the duplicate rule's action (Block vs. Alert/Report) be confirmed before a specific bulk import, rather than left at whatever the default is?
options: Duplicate rule actions cannot be changed once set and apply identically to every import forever
Because the right action depends on context — a clean first load wants Block, while an import expected to have legitimate near-matches wants Alert or Report
Block is always correct and Alert/Report should never be used for imports
The action only matters for manual data entry, never for bulk imports
questions.explain: The checklist calls for confirming the action deliberately each time, since the right choice depends on what the specific import is expected to contain.
